assumptions: source assumption: minimum-energy escape with no atmosphere — the object just comes to rest at infinity (v₂ = 0, U → 0), so total energy is zero and ½·m·v_esc² = G·M·m/R (§13.3 derivation).

models.inverse_notes: Reference radius solves as R = 2*6.67e-11*M/v2; substitution check with the NASA escape value (v2 = (11186 m/s)², M = 5.96e24 kg) returns R = 6.3545e6 m against 6.37e6 m (0.2%, within oracle rounding). Mass solves as M = v2*R/(2*6.67e-11). Requires v2 > 0 beyond the declared output domain. Do not publish rearrangements as separate records.
limitations: Minimum-energy, no-atmosphere idealization; real launches need more (gravity and drag losses, rotation assist — the source discusses both qualitatively).
Two-body energy threshold only; post-escape trajectory (hyperbolic excess, targeting) is out of lane.
Not a circular-orbit speed: escape speed is exactly √2 larger than the circular speed at the same radius — do not interchange the records.
